source_evidence: Funds pass along these costs to investors by deducting fees and expenses from NAV. That means you pay the fees and expenses indirectly.
answer: ETF fees and expenses are costs of running the fund. The fund deducts them from its net asset value (NAV), so investors pay them indirectly. Costs vary from one ETF to another, and even small fee differences can lead to large differences in returns over time. A fund with higher costs must perform better than a lower-cost fund to produce the same returns for investors.
